purpose: A method for building and maintaining a granular, locally-tuned category taxonomy of Turlock and Stanislaus County independent businesses — fine enough that each category grounds one category specialist — by starting from a NAICS-informed but locally expanded scheme, applying explicit split/merge rules tuned to the real ag/dairy and Assyrian/Portuguese/Mexican/South-Asian local mix, assigning each business a primary plus optional secondary categories, mapping every category to exactly one owning specialist, estimating size only as a labeled benchmark band from public signals, and versioning the taxonomy forward as discovery reveals new clusters.
assumptions: no observed business registry is supplied; categories, count bands, and scores are reasoned heuristic priors, not a census
the unit being categorized is an independent (non-chain, locally owned) business operating in Turlock or the surrounding Stanislaus County trade area
the local economy is ag/dairy-heavy with notable Assyrian, Portuguese/Azorean, Mexican, and Punjabi/South-Asian communities that shape the real business mix
only public business data is used: storefront signage, public listings, NAICS codes, and county Fictitious Business Name filings — never private owner or financial records
per-business revenue is not public for private shops and is modeled only as a labeled estimate, never stated as actual
exclusions: chain and franchise outlets whose categorization is dictated by a national brand rather than local character
income strategy for individual workers and the wage-job ladder — covered by a separate KB
the deep operating playbook of any single category — owned by that category's own specialist, not this taxonomy
private financial statements, tax records, or personal data about owners beyond public Fictitious Business Name filings
businesses physically outside the Turlock / Stanislaus County trade area
source_description: heuristic prior estimates for a Turlock independent-business category taxonomy, informed by the U.S. Census NAICS structure, general knowledge of Stanislaus County's ag/dairy economy and its Assyrian, Portuguese/Azorean, Mexican, and Punjabi/South-Asian communities, and public business-listing conventions; no supplied registry or census
source_citation: U.S. Census Bureau North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) 2022; California Secretary of State and Stanislaus County Clerk-Recorder Fictitious Business Name (FBN) filing practice; general public knowledge of Turlock/Stanislaus County industry mix and ethnic-community business clusters; heuristic priors where no dataset is supplied

competency_questions.question: Why must the taxonomy be deliberately granular rather than generalized, and how does each category map to a specialist?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: TAXONOMY_GOAL states that granularity is what lets each category ground one category specialist, and CATEGORY_SPECIALIST_MAP gives the one-category-to-one-specialist rule

competency_questions.question: What base classification scheme does the taxonomy start from and how is it expanded for local reality?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: BASE_SCHEME names NAICS as the spine and explains the local-expansion principle that favors granularity over generalization

competency_questions.question: When is a category split into finer ones versus when are thin categories merged, and what is the target band?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: GRANULARITY_RULE gives a businesses-per-category target band and the split and merge triggers around it

competency_questions.question: How is food retail split so that a panaderia, European bakery, donut shop, tortilleria, and ethnic-sweets shop are distinct, and how are ethnic-community grocers split by community?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: FOOD_RETAIL_SPLIT enumerates the distinct baked-goods/food-retail categories with their separating signal and ETHNIC_GROCERS separates Assyrian/Middle-Eastern, Portuguese/Azorean, Mexican, Punjabi/South-Asian, and Halal grocers tied to local communities

competency_questions.question: How are restaurants categorized by both cuisine and service format?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: RESTAURANTS_SPLIT defines the cuisine-by-format grid (taqueria, sit-down ethnic, cafe/coffeehouse, drive-thru, food truck, bakery-cafe)

competency_questions.question: How are personal-care and automotive service businesses split into trade-specific categories?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: PERSONAL_CARE splits hair/barber/nail/spa/tattoo and AUTOMOTIVE_TRADES splits mechanical/body/tires/detail/smog/parts

competency_questions.question: How are independent health-and-wellness practices and professional/financial services categorized?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: HEALTH_WELLNESS splits chiro/dental/optometry/PT/studios and PROF_FINANCIAL splits accounting/legal/insurance/real-estate/notary-immigration

competency_questions.question: How is the retail-goods space split into boutique-level categories?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: RETAIL_GOODS separates apparel, jewelry, antiques/vintage, home decor, gifts/specialty, smoke/vape, and thrift/consignment

competency_questions.question: How are contractor/building trades and the ag/dairy-support businesses categorized for Turlock?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: CONTRACTOR_TRADES splits general/landscape/MEP/flooring/signage and AG_DAIRY_SUPPORT covers feed/equipment/large-animal-vet/ag-services central to the local economy

competency_questions.question: How are specialty/hobby retail and small food-production/wholesale businesses categorized?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SPECIALTY_HOBBY covers florist/bike/music/pet and FOOD_PRODUCTION covers commercial bakers/roasters/packagers/cottage-food makers

competency_questions.question: How is a business that spans several categories handled?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: MULTI_CATEGORY assigns exactly one primary category plus optional secondary categories with a rule for choosing the primary

competency_questions.question: How are ambiguous or edge assignments decided and tie-broken?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: EDGE_ASSIGNMENT gives the decision order and explicit tie-break rules for businesses that resist a single category

competency_questions.question: How is size or revenue represented honestly given that per-business revenue is not public?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: REVENUE_ESTIMATION models revenue only as a labeled benchmark band scaled by observable size signals, tagged estimate-not-actual with a confidence level, and PUBLIC_DATA_GUARDRAIL forbids stating any dollar figure as fact

competency_questions.question: How are category names and stable ids assigned, and how does the taxonomy evolve as new clusters are discovered without silently re-generalizing?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: NAMING_IDS gives the naming convention and a stable-id rule that survives renames/merges, and VERSIONING adds categories on discovery, records the change, and forbids silent re-merging of previously split categories

glossary.definition: North American Industry Classification System: the federal 6-digit industry coding spine the taxonomy starts from, then expands locally because NAICS leaf codes are too coarse to ground a Turlock-specific category specialist.

One autonomous specialist that owns a single category — its operators, pay structure, supply chain, and local nuance — which is why each category must be narrow enough to brief one specialist without overlap.

A Fictitious Business Name statement filed with the Stanislaus County Clerk-Recorder: a public record giving a business's operating name, address, and registrant, used here as the only sanctioned owner-linked source.
The target count of real local businesses a healthy category should hold (a small band, not one and not hundreds); too many triggers a split, too few triggers a merge or a watch-list hold.
The single category a multi-line business is filed under, chosen by its dominant revenue-driving activity, with any other lines recorded as secondary categories that do not own the business.
An industry-typical revenue figure per worker (or per square foot) used only to scale observable size signals into a labeled revenue estimate band — never a measured figure for a named shop.

A publicly observable proxy for scale — storefront square footage, visible employee count, number of service bays or chairs, parking/seating — used to place a business in a size tier without any private financial data.
A short immutable code assigned to a category at creation that never changes even when the display name is reworded, so downstream specialist assignments and history survive renames.

A dedicated tortilla and masa producer/retailer, kept distinct from a panaderia (sweet bread bakery) and a full Mexican grocery because its product, equipment, and operator profile differ enough to warrant its own category and specialist.

A California Cottage Food Operation: a home-based maker of approved low-risk foods sold under a permit, categorized separately from commercial production because its scale, regulation, and channel differ sharply.

nodes.definition: Set the governing aim: produce categories fine-grained enough that each one is a coherent, briefable domain a single category specialist can fully own, yet broad enough to hold more than a single business. The taxonomy is not a filing convenience; it is the index that decides how many specialists exist and what each is accountable for, so every category boundary is really a specialist boundary.

included: the granularity-as-specialist-boundary principle
category coherence and brief-ability test
the dual fine-enough/broad-enough constraint

pros.claim: Treating each category as a specialist boundary forces categories to be coherent enough to brief and own
pros.example: splitting 'food' into panaderia, tortilleria, and donut shop because no single operator profile spans all three

cons.claim: Optimizing categories for specialist-ownership can fragment the map beyond what a small market sustains
cons.example: minting a standalone category for a single accordion-repair shop that no specialist can stay busy on

failure_modes: categories so broad a specialist cannot speak with authority on any member
categories so narrow most hold a single business and no specialist is justified
acceptance_tests: the goal statement ties category granularity explicitly to one-specialist-per-category and states both the fine-enough and broad-enough bounds
revisit_triggers: the count of viable specialists the project can support changes
a category proves un-briefable as one coherent domain

base.update_signal: the taxonomy's purpose or the supported specialist count is restated

nodes.definition: Adopt NAICS as the structural spine — its sectors and subsectors give a defensible, recognized starting partition — but treat its leaf codes as a floor, not the answer, because they group too coarsely for local use (one NAICS code lumps every 'limited-service restaurant' together). Expand each relevant branch into finer locally-meaningful categories, deliberately choosing granularity over generalization wherever Turlock's mix shows a real distinction NAICS hides.

included: NAICS as the recognized spine
leaf codes as a floor to expand
the granularity-over-generalization expansion principle

pros.claim: Anchoring to NAICS keeps the taxonomy mappable to external data while local expansion keeps it useful
pros.example: starting from NAICS 722515 then splitting it into coffeehouse, bakery-cafe, and donut-shop categories

cons.claim: Diverging from NAICS leaf codes breaks one-to-one mapping to census/industry datasets
cons.example: a local 'tortilleria' category that no single NAICS code reports, complicating benchmark lookups

failure_modes: stopping at NAICS leaves and inheriting their over-generalization
expanding so far from NAICS that no external benchmark can be attached
acceptance_tests: the scheme names NAICS as the spine, declares leaf codes a floor, and states the granularity-over-generalization expansion rule with at least one worked local expansion
revisit_triggers: NAICS is revised
a local distinction emerges that no current branch captures

base.update_signal: the NAICS revision or the local-expansion principle changes

nodes.definition: Make granularity decidable with a count rule: a healthy category holds a small band of real local businesses (roughly a handful up to a couple dozen). Split a category when it grows past the upper bound or when its members clearly divide by operator profile, supply chain, or community served; merge or hold thin categories below the lower bound unless they are genuinely distinct domains worth a specialist. The band, not taste, drives split/merge.

included: the businesses-per-category target band
split triggers (size or internal divergence)
merge/hold triggers for thin categories

pros.claim: A numeric band makes split/merge auditable instead of a matter of opinion
pros.example: splitting 'auto services' once it exceeds the band and divides cleanly into repair vs body vs tires

cons.claim: A pure count band can over-split a large but homogeneous category or strand a tiny but distinct one
cons.example: forcing a split of thirty near-identical taquerias that share one operator profile

failure_modes: splitting on count alone when members are homogeneous
merging a thin but genuinely distinct category just to clear the lower bound
acceptance_tests: the rule states a businesses-per-category band and the explicit triggers that fire a split versus a merge/hold
revisit_triggers: the local business population grows or shrinks materially
a category repeatedly sits at a band boundary

base.update_signal: the count band or a split/merge trigger threshold changes

nodes.definition: Govern identity: each category gets a short human display name following a fixed convention (community/cuisine qualifier + product/service noun + format where it matters, e.g. 'Mexican Panaderia', 'Auto Body & Collision') and a separate immutable stable id assigned at creation. The display name may be reworded for clarity; the stable id never changes, so specialist assignments, history, and prior assignments survive renames, splits, and merges without breaking references.

included: display-name convention
immutable stable category id
how ids survive renames/splits/merges

pros.claim: Separating a mutable name from an immutable id lets categories be reworded without orphaning assignments
pros.example: renaming 'Hair Salon' to 'Hair Salon & Color Studio' while the stable id keeps every assigned shop attached

cons.claim: A rigid naming convention can read awkwardly for hybrid businesses that resist a single noun
cons.example: a bakery-cafe-roaster whose convention-built name becomes a clumsy three-part label

failure_modes: reusing a retired id for a new category and corrupting history
encoding mutable attributes into the stable id so it must change
acceptance_tests: the convention is stated, every category carries an immutable stable id distinct from its display name, and the rule for ids surviving splits/merges is given
revisit_triggers: the naming convention is revised
an id collision or reuse is detected

base.update_signal: the naming convention or id-assignment rule changes

nodes.definition: Split prepared-food retail finely because Turlock's mix hides several distinct operator profiles inside NAICS 'bakery': a Mexican panaderia (sweet breads, conchas, custom pan dulce), a European/specialty bakery (pastry, wedding cakes, artisan bread), a donut shop (often family-run, early-morning, fryer-based), a tortilleria (masa and tortillas, distinct equipment), and an ethnic-sweets shop (Assyrian/Middle-Eastern baklava and pastries, or Indian mithai). Each differs in product, equipment, supply chain, and community, so each is its own category.

included: panaderia, European/specialty bakery, donut shop, tortilleria, ethnic-sweets as distinct categories
the product/equipment/community signal that separates them

pros.claim: Splitting by product and operator profile gives each baked-goods category a specialist who actually knows its trade
pros.example: a panaderia specialist who understands pan dulce demand cycles, distinct from a wedding-cake bakery specialist

cons.claim: Fine baked-goods splits create boundary cases for hybrids that bake several traditions
cons.example: a shop selling both conchas and baklava that fits two categories at once

failure_modes: collapsing a tortilleria into a generic bakery and losing its distinct supply chain
treating a donut shop and a pastry bakery as one because both 'bake'
acceptance_tests: at least five distinct food-retail categories are named (panaderia, European/specialty bakery, donut shop, tortilleria, ethnic sweets) each with its separating product/operator signal
revisit_triggers: a new baked-goods tradition opens locally
a hybrid shop forces a boundary clarification

base.update_signal: a new food-retail tradition or hybrid forces a category change

nodes.definition: Split independent grocers by the community they primarily serve, because Turlock's distinct populations sustain distinct stores with different inventory, suppliers, and clientele: Assyrian/Middle-Eastern markets (Turlock has a large Assyrian community), Portuguese/Azorean markets (linguica, cheeses, dairy-region staples), Mexican mercados/carnicerias, Punjabi/South-Asian grocers (spices, lentils, halal-adjacent goods), and dedicated Halal markets (which may cut across communities). Community of service, not just 'grocery', is the splitting axis.

included: Assyrian/Middle-Eastern, Portuguese/Azorean, Mexican, Punjabi/South-Asian, and Halal grocer categories
community-of-service as the splitting axis

pros.claim: Splitting grocers by community matches the real supplier and clientele differences a specialist must know
pros.example: an Assyrian-market specialist who tracks Middle-Eastern importers, distinct from a Mexican-mercado specialist

cons.claim: Community-keyed categories blur when a store serves several communities or relabels to broaden appeal
cons.example: a 'Mediterranean & Indian' market that genuinely straddles two community categories

failure_modes: lumping all ethnic grocers into one and erasing supplier-level distinctions
assigning a multi-community store to one category without recording the secondary
acceptance_tests: at least five community-keyed grocer categories are named (Assyrian/Middle-Eastern, Portuguese/Azorean, Mexican, Punjabi/South-Asian, Halal) with community-of-service stated as the splitting axis
revisit_triggers: a community's local population or store count shifts
a multi-community store forces a primary/secondary decision

base.update_signal: a community's store cluster or a multi-community store changes the split

nodes.definition: Categorize restaurants on two axes at once — cuisine and service format — because both shape the operator and the specialist needed: a taqueria, a sit-down ethnic restaurant (Assyrian, Portuguese, Mexican, Indian, etc.), a cafe/coffeehouse, a drive-thru, a food truck, and a bakery-cafe are genuinely different businesses even at the same cuisine. The category is the cuisine-by-format cell that best fits the dominant service model, with cuisine recorded so a specialist sees both.

included: taqueria, sit-down ethnic, cafe/coffeehouse, drive-thru, food truck, bakery-cafe formats
cuisine recorded alongside format

pros.claim: Splitting on cuisine and format captures that a taqueria and a sit-down Mexican restaurant need different specialists
pros.example: a food-truck specialist who knows permitting and routes, distinct from a sit-down-restaurant specialist

cons.claim: A two-axis grid multiplies categories and can produce nearly empty cuisine-by-format cells
cons.example: a single Portuguese food truck occupying its own otherwise-empty cell

failure_modes: collapsing format so a food truck and a sit-down restaurant share a category
splitting every cuisine-by-format cell even when most are empty
acceptance_tests: the six service formats are defined and the rule records cuisine alongside the format-driven category
revisit_triggers: a new cuisine or format cluster appears
an empty cuisine-by-format cell needs collapsing

base.update_signal: a new cuisine/format cluster or an empty cell forces a change

nodes.definition: Split personal-care services by the licensed trade and operator profile rather than lumping them as 'beauty': hair salon, barber shop (distinct license and clientele), nail salon, spa/esthetics (facials, waxing, skin), and tattoo/piercing studio (separate health-permit regime). Each has its own licensing, supply chain, booth-rental economics, and community footprint, so each grounds a separate specialist.

included: hair salon, barber, nail salon, spa/esthetics, tattoo/piercing as distinct categories
license and operator-profile as the split axis

pros.claim: Splitting by license matches the distinct regulation and chair/booth economics each trade runs on
pros.example: a nail-salon specialist who knows ventilation rules and product supply, distinct from a barber specialist

cons.claim: Combined salon-and-spa businesses straddle two categories and force a primary choice
cons.example: a full salon that also offers facials and waxing under one roof

failure_modes: merging barber and hair salon despite different licenses and clientele
filing a tattoo studio under generic personal care and missing its health-permit regime
acceptance_tests: at least five personal-care categories are named (hair, barber, nail, spa/esthetics, tattoo/piercing) each tied to its license/operator profile
revisit_triggers: a licensing regime changes
a combined salon-spa forces a primary/secondary decision

base.update_signal: a personal-care licensing change or hybrid shop forces a change

nodes.definition: Split automotive services by the actual trade because skills, equipment, and parts supply diverge sharply: mechanical/general repair, body/collision (paint booths, insurance work), tires/wheels, detailing, smog check/inspection (state-licensed stations), and auto parts retail. A general repair shop, a collision center, and a smog station share almost no operating knowledge, so each is its own category and specialist.

included: mechanical repair, body/collision, tires/wheels, detailing, smog/inspection, auto parts as distinct categories
trade-specific equipment and licensing as the split axis

pros.claim: Trade-level splits match the distinct licensing and parts supply each automotive sub-trade requires
pros.example: a smog-station specialist who knows BAR licensing, distinct from a collision-center specialist handling insurance estimates

cons.claim: Multi-service shops doing repair, tires, and smog under one roof straddle several categories
cons.example: a one-stop shop that does general repair plus smog plus tires

failure_modes: lumping body and mechanical repair despite different equipment and insurance dynamics
missing that smog/inspection is a separately licensed category
acceptance_tests: at least six automotive categories are named (mechanical, body/collision, tires, detailing, smog/inspection, parts) each with its distinguishing trade or license
revisit_triggers: a state inspection/BAR rule changes
a multi-service shop forces a primary/secondary split

base.update_signal: an automotive licensing change or multi-service shop forces a change

nodes.definition: Categorize independent (non-hospital) health and wellness practices by discipline: chiropractic, dental, optometry, physical therapy, and independent gyms/fitness studios (CrossFit boxes, yoga, martial arts, dance). Each is a licensed or distinct-format practice with its own referral patterns, insurance posture, and operator profile, so a single 'health' bucket would be useless to a specialist; the line stops short of hospital-employed providers.

included: chiropractic, dental, optometry, physical therapy, independent gyms/studios
independent (non-hospital) practices only

pros.claim: Discipline-level splits match distinct licensing and insurance dynamics each practice runs on
pros.example: an independent-gym specialist who knows membership economics, distinct from a dental-practice specialist handling insurance billing

cons.claim: Multidisciplinary wellness clinics (chiro plus PT plus massage) blur the discipline split
cons.example: a clinic offering chiropractic and physical therapy under one license group

failure_modes: filing an independent studio under retail or services and missing its membership model
lumping optometry and dental as one 'medical' category
acceptance_tests: at least five health/wellness categories are named (chiro, dental, optometry, PT, independent gyms/studios) with independent-practice scope stated
revisit_triggers: a new independent practice type clusters locally
a multidisciplinary clinic forces a primary/secondary decision

base.update_signal: a new independent-practice cluster or multidisciplinary clinic forces a change

nodes.definition: Split independent professional and financial services by practice: accounting/tax preparation, legal practice, insurance brokerage, real-estate brokerage, and notary/immigration-document services (notarios, document preparers — a real and locally significant category serving immigrant communities, distinct from licensed legal practice). Each has its own credentialing, client base, and seasonality, and the notary/immigration-doc line must be kept distinct from legal practice to avoid conflating regulated roles.

included: accounting/tax, legal, insurance brokerage, real-estate brokerage, notary/immigration-doc as distinct categories
credentialing and client base as the split axis

pros.claim: Separating notary/immigration-doc from legal practice respects the regulatory line between the two
pros.example: a document-preparation specialist who knows the scope limits notarios must observe, distinct from a licensed-attorney specialist

cons.claim: Solo practitioners often blend roles (an accountant who also does notary and insurance), blurring the split
cons.example: a tax preparer who also runs an insurance side-line and notarizes documents

failure_modes: conflating notary/document services with licensed legal practice
lumping accounting and insurance because both are 'financial'
acceptance_tests: at least five professional/financial categories are named (accounting/tax, legal, insurance, real estate, notary/immigration-doc) with the legal-versus-notario line drawn
revisit_triggers: a credentialing or document-preparer regulation changes
a blended solo practice forces a primary/secondary decision

base.update_signal: a professional credentialing rule or blended practice forces a change

nodes.definition: Split independent goods retail into boutique-level categories rather than one 'store' bucket: apparel boutique, jewelry, antiques/vintage, home decor/furnishings, gifts/specialty, smoke/vape shop, and thrift/consignment. Inventory model, sourcing, margin, and clientele differ enough per category to ground distinct specialists; thrift/consignment in particular runs a fundamentally different sourcing model (donated/consigned stock) than new-goods retail.

included: apparel, jewelry, antiques/vintage, home decor, gifts/specialty, smoke/vape, thrift/consignment
inventory and sourcing model as the split axis

pros.claim: Splitting by sourcing and inventory model separates new-goods boutiques from consignment-driven resale
pros.example: a thrift/consignment specialist who understands donated-stock flow, distinct from an apparel-boutique buyer specialist

cons.claim: Eclectic shops mixing gifts, decor, and vintage resist a single retail category
cons.example: a store selling new gifts, vintage furniture, and consigned clothing together

failure_modes: lumping thrift/consignment with new-goods retail and erasing its sourcing model
merging antiques and home decor despite different sourcing and clientele
acceptance_tests: at least seven retail-goods categories are named (apparel, jewelry, antiques/vintage, home decor, gifts/specialty, smoke/vape, thrift/consignment) with the sourcing/inventory split axis stated
revisit_triggers: a new retail niche clusters locally
an eclectic shop forces a primary/secondary decision

base.update_signal: a new retail niche or eclectic shop forces a change

nodes.definition: Categorize building and contractor trades by the licensed specialty, since each holds a distinct contractor classification and operating model: general contractor, landscaping/grounds, the MEP cluster (HVAC, plumbing, electrical — each its own license), flooring, and signage. These are largely mobile/project businesses rather than storefronts, so the size signals differ, but the licensed-specialty split is the same granularity-over-generalization move applied to trades.

included: general, landscaping, HVAC/plumbing/electrical, flooring, signage as distinct categories
license classification as the split axis

pros.claim: Splitting by contractor license matches the distinct bidding, bonding, and crew models each trade runs
pros.example: an electrical-contractor specialist who knows licensing and permit flow, distinct from a landscaping-crew specialist

cons.claim: Design-build generals subcontract several trades, blurring where they sit
cons.example: a general contractor who self-performs flooring and signage on its own jobs

failure_modes: lumping HVAC, plumbing, and electrical as one 'MEP' category despite separate licenses
missing that signage is a distinct fabrication-and-install trade
acceptance_tests: at least five contractor categories are named (general, landscaping, HVAC/plumbing/electrical, flooring, signage) with license classification as the split axis
revisit_triggers: a contractor licensing classification changes
a design-build firm forces a primary/secondary decision

base.update_signal: a contractor licensing change or design-build firm forces a change

nodes.definition: Carve the ag-adjacent and dairy-support businesses that are central to Turlock and missing from any generic taxonomy: feed/farm-supply stores, ag-equipment dealers and repair (tractors, irrigation, milking systems), large-animal/dairy veterinary practices, and ag services (custom harvesting, hauling, crop-input/agronomy suppliers, dairy nutrition). This is the local economic backbone, so these get first-class categories rather than being buried under generic retail or services.

included: feed/farm supply, ag-equipment dealers and repair, large-animal/dairy vet, ag services as distinct categories
first-class treatment given local economic centrality
excluded: the farms and dairies themselves as production operations

pros.claim: First-class ag/dairy-support categories capture the actual backbone of the Turlock economy
pros.example: a dairy-equipment-repair specialist who knows milking-system service, distinct from a consumer auto specialist

cons.claim: Ag-support businesses can be seasonal or serve a wide rural area, blurring the Turlock trade-area boundary
cons.example: a custom-harvest operator based near Turlock but working three counties

failure_modes: burying feed/farm supply under generic hardware or retail
missing the large-animal vet as distinct from a small-animal clinic
acceptance_tests: at least four ag/dairy-support categories are named (feed/farm supply, ag equipment + repair, large-animal/dairy vet, ag services) with their local-centrality rationale stated
revisit_triggers: a dairy or ag-sector shift changes which support businesses cluster
the trade-area boundary for a mobile ag service needs a ruling

base.update_signal: a dairy/ag-sector shift changes the support-business cluster

nodes.definition: Group the specialty and hobby businesses that are individually small but each distinct: florist, bike shop (sales plus repair), music/instruments (sales, lessons, repair), and pet supply/grooming. Each serves a narrow enthusiast or occasion-driven market with its own sourcing and service mix; they are kept as separate thin categories where genuinely distinct, and are the canonical place to apply the merge rule when any one falls below the count band.

included: florist, bike shop, music/instruments, pet supply/grooming as distinct categories
thin-but-distinct treatment and merge candidacy

pros.claim: Naming thin hobby categories distinctly preserves their specialist value while flagging them for the merge rule
pros.example: a bike-shop specialist who knows repair-service margins, kept distinct unless the category falls below the band

cons.claim: Several of these are perennially sub-band, tempting over-merging that erases real distinctions
cons.example: merging florist and gift shop because each is small, losing the florist's perishable-supply model

failure_modes: merging genuinely distinct hobby categories just to clear the count band
splitting pet supply from grooming when one operator does both at sub-band scale
acceptance_tests: at least four specialty/hobby categories are named (florist, bike, music/instruments, pet supply/grooming) with their thin-but-distinct and merge-candidacy status stated
revisit_triggers: a hobby category falls below or rises above the count band
a combined hobby shop forces a primary/secondary decision

base.update_signal: a hobby category crosses the count band or a combined shop forces a change

nodes.definition: Categorize the production/wholesale side of food separately from retail: commercial bakers selling wholesale, coffee roasters, packagers/co-packers, and cottage-food makers (California Cottage Food Operation home producers). These sell business-to-business or under home-based permits rather than over a retail counter, so their scale, regulation, and channel differ sharply and they cannot share a category with the storefront food-retail categories.

included: commercial wholesale bakers, roasters, packagers/co-packers, cottage-food makers
production/wholesale channel as the split axis from retail

pros.claim: Separating production/wholesale from retail matches the B2B channel and permit regime a specialist must know
pros.example: a cottage-food specialist who knows CDPH permit limits, distinct from a storefront-bakery specialist

cons.claim: Hybrid makers sell both wholesale and over a counter, straddling production and retail categories
cons.example: a roaster that wholesales beans and also runs a retail cafe counter

failure_modes: filing a wholesale baker under storefront bakery and missing its B2B channel
treating a cottage-food maker as a full commercial producer
acceptance_tests: at least four production/wholesale categories are named (commercial bakers, roasters, packagers, cottage-food makers) with the production-versus-retail channel split stated
revisit_triggers: a cottage-food or co-packing regulation changes
a hybrid wholesale-and-retail maker forces a primary/secondary decision

base.update_signal: a production/cottage-food regulation or hybrid maker forces a change

nodes.definition: Handle businesses that genuinely span categories with a primary-plus-secondary rule: assign exactly one primary category chosen by the dominant revenue-driving activity (judged from public size signals, not private financials), and record any other real lines as secondary categories that inform but do not own the business. The primary determines which specialist owns the business; secondaries flag cross-cutting relevance and prevent the multi-line business from vanishing from a sibling category's view.

included: one primary by dominant activity
optional secondary categories
primary determines ownership
excluded: the specialist-merge rule for thin categories

pros.claim: A single primary keeps ownership unambiguous while secondaries preserve cross-cutting visibility
pros.example: a panaderia that also runs a taqueria counter filed primary as panaderia, secondary as taqueria

cons.claim: Choosing the dominant activity from public signals alone can misrank two near-equal lines
cons.example: a market and grill split roughly evenly with no public way to tell which drives more revenue

failure_modes: assigning two co-equal primaries and breaking one-business-one-owner
dropping secondary lines so a multi-line business disappears from a sibling category
acceptance_tests: each multi-line business has exactly one primary category by dominant activity plus zero or more recorded secondaries, and the primary is the owning category
revisit_triggers: a business's dominant line shifts
a near-tie between two lines needs the edge-assignment tie-break

base.update_signal: a multi-line business's dominant activity or secondary set changes

nodes.definition: Estimate a business's scale only as a clearly labeled band, never as a stated dollar fact: take an industry revenue-per-employee or revenue-per-square-foot benchmark for the category and scale it by publicly observable size signals (storefront footage, visible staff/chairs/bays, seating), producing a wide low/high band tagged 'estimate, not actual' with a confidence level and a note of what public evidence would tighten or confirm it. No named business is ever assigned an actual revenue figure.

included: benchmark-times-size-signal estimation
low/high band with a confidence level
the estimate-not-actual label and confirming-evidence note
excluded: any actual revenue figure for a named business

pros.claim: A labeled benchmark band conveys relative scale without ever fabricating a private business's revenue
pros.example: labeling a salon 'estimated $X-$Y/yr, low confidence, from chair count and benchmark, not actual'

cons.claim: Benchmark-scaled bands can be wide enough to look uninformative for small or atypical shops
cons.example: a niche tortilleria whose revenue-per-employee diverges far from the generic food-retail benchmark

failure_modes: dropping the estimate label so a band reads as a stated fact
scaling by a benchmark from a different category and producing a misleading band
acceptance_tests: every revenue figure for a named business is a low/high band carrying an explicit estimate-not-actual tag, a confidence level, and a note of what would confirm it
revisit_triggers: a category benchmark is updated
a new public size signal sharpens or changes the estimate

base.update_signal: a benchmark or a public size signal behind an estimate changes

nodes.definition: Bound every assignment and estimate to public data only: storefront observation, public listings and signage, NAICS codes, and Stanislaus County Fictitious Business Name filings for owner/operating-name linkage. It forbids stating any dollar revenue for a named business as fact, using non-public financial or tax records, and recording private personal data about owners beyond what an FBN filing already makes public. This is the honesty floor the whole taxonomy stands on.

included: public-data-only sourcing
no actual-revenue claims for named businesses
no private owner data beyond FBN public records
excluded: the mechanics of the benchmark band

pros.claim: A hard public-data floor prevents the taxonomy from ever fabricating or exposing private business information
pros.example: linking an operating name to a registrant only via the public FBN filing, never via private records

cons.claim: Restricting to public data leaves real gaps the taxonomy must mark as unknown rather than fill
cons.example: an unincorporated home business with no FBN filing and no public footprint to categorize from

failure_modes: stating a benchmark band as if it were the business's actual revenue
recording owner personal data that exceeds the public FBN record
acceptance_tests: every datum used traces to a public source, no named business carries an actual-revenue claim, and no owner data exceeds public FBN filings
revisit_triggers: a new public data source becomes available
a sourcing or privacy boundary is challenged

base.update_signal: a public data source or a privacy boundary changes

nodes.definition: Resolve businesses that resist a single category with an explicit decision order: try the dominant-activity rule first; if two lines are near-equal, break the tie by (1) which category is under-served and needs the data, (2) which matches the FBN-filed primary purpose, then (3) which the storefront signage leads with. If still unresolved, assign the broader parent category and open a watch-list note rather than guessing a fine leaf. Every ambiguous call records its reason.

included: the ordered decision rules
explicit tie-breaks (under-served, FBN purpose, signage)
fallback to parent category with a recorded reason

pros.claim: A fixed tie-break order makes ambiguous assignments reproducible and auditable
pros.example: two equal lines resolved to the under-served category and stamped with the reason

cons.claim: An under-served tie-break can bias assignments toward thin categories and distort their counts
cons.example: repeatedly routing borderline shops into a sparse category until it looks artificially healthy

failure_modes: guessing a fine leaf for a genuinely ambiguous business instead of holding at the parent
leaving an ambiguous call unrecorded so it cannot be revisited
acceptance_tests: the decision order and at least three named tie-breaks are stated, with a parent-category fallback and a required recorded reason for every ambiguous call
revisit_triggers: a tie-break rule produces a biased distribution
a held parent-category business gains enough signal to place at a leaf

base.update_signal: a tie-break rule or its observed distribution changes

nodes.definition: Bind the taxonomy to the specialist roster with a one-category-to-one-specialist rule: every category maps to exactly one owning specialist, and one specialist may own a small set of genuinely thin sibling categories only when none alone justifies a dedicated specialist. The mapping is what turns the category map into a work assignment; it forces the granularity rule to stay honest, because a category that cannot justify or share a specialist is a sign it was mis-split or mis-merged.

included: one category to one owning specialist
permitted bundling of thin siblings under one specialist
the mapping as a check on granularity

pros.claim: An explicit one-to-one map makes every category accountable to exactly one owner and exposes mis-splits
pros.example: merging florist and balloon-decor under one specialist because neither sustains a dedicated owner

cons.claim: Bundling thin siblings under one specialist can overload that specialist or blur its expertise
cons.example: one specialist owning bike, music, and pet shops with little shared knowledge

failure_modes: two specialists claiming the same category and duplicating ownership
a category with no specialist and no eligible bundle left unowned
acceptance_tests: every category maps to exactly one owning specialist, and any specialist owning multiple categories owns only genuinely thin, related siblings
revisit_triggers: a category is split or merged
a specialist is added, retired, or overloaded

base.update_signal: a category split/merge or a specialist roster change occurs

nodes.definition: Keep the taxonomy a living, append-forward artifact: add a new category whenever discovery reveals a real cluster the current map cannot hold, record the change with a version stamp and rationale, and migrate affected assignments by stable id. The hard rule is no silent re-generalization — a previously justified split is never quietly re-merged; any merge must be explicit, versioned, and justified, so the map only ever gets more accurate, not lazily coarser.

included: append-on-discovery of new categories
versioned, justified changes migrated by stable id
the no-silent-regeneralization rule

pros.claim: Append-forward versioning lets the taxonomy track a changing local economy without losing history
pros.example: adding a 'boba/tea shop' category when a cluster emerges, stamped and migrated by stable id

cons.claim: Strict no-regeneralization can leave obsolete fine categories lingering after a niche dies out
cons.example: a video-rental category kept long after the last local store closed

failure_modes: silently re-merging split categories and erasing a real distinction
adding categories without version stamps so change history is lost
acceptance_tests: new categories are added with a version stamp and rationale, migrated by stable id, and no previously justified split is merged without an explicit versioned justification
revisit_triggers: a new business cluster is discovered
a category becomes obsolete and a merge is proposed

base.update_signal: a new cluster is discovered or a merge is proposed

edges.why_related: the goal of specialist-grounding categories sets why the base scheme must expand NAICS rather than stop at it
the one-category-one-specialist mapping operationalizes the goal that each category grounds a specialist
the count-band split/merge rule operates on the expanded NAICS scheme as its substrate
names and stable ids are assigned to the categories the base scheme defines
the food-retail split is the granularity rule applied to the bakery/food-retail branch
the grocer split applies the granularity rule along the community-of-service axis
the restaurant cuisine-by-format grid applies the granularity rule to food service
personal-care categories are the granularity rule applied along licensed-trade lines
the automotive split applies the granularity rule across distinct vehicle trades
health/wellness disciplines are split by the granularity rule along practice lines
professional/financial categories apply the granularity rule by credentialed practice
the retail-goods boutique split applies the granularity rule by sourcing/inventory model
contractor categories apply the granularity rule along license classifications
ag/dairy-support categories apply the granularity rule to the local economic backbone
specialty/hobby categories apply the granularity rule to thin enthusiast niches
production/wholesale food categories apply the granularity rule along the B2B channel
multi-line food-retail businesses need a primary chosen from the food-retail categories
multi-community grocers feed the primary/secondary assignment rule
restaurants with retail or production side-lines need a primary from the restaurant categories
combined salon-spa businesses need a primary from the personal-care categories
multi-service auto shops need a primary from the automotive categories
multidisciplinary clinics need a primary from the health/wellness categories
blended solo practices need a primary from the professional/financial categories
eclectic shops need a primary from the retail-goods categories
design-build firms need a primary from the contractor categories
ag-support businesses with retail counters need a primary from the ag categories
combined hobby shops need a primary from the specialty categories
hybrid wholesale-and-retail makers need a primary from the production categories
the dominant-activity primary fixes which category benchmark scales the revenue band
the revenue band must sit under the public-data-only honesty floor that forbids stated dollar facts
ambiguous primary choices fall through to the edge-assignment tie-break protocol
only after assignment is resolved can a category be mapped to its owning specialist
the specialist map both consumes and checks the granularity rule's split/merge outcomes
versioning migrates specialist ownership when categories are added, split, or merged
versioned migrations rely on the stable ids to carry assignments across renames and splits
discovering a new cluster on a version pass feeds back into a fresh split/merge evaluation
the count band pressures thin hobby categories toward merging while their distinct operator profiles argue for keeping them split
edges.resolution_rule: keep a sub-band hobby category split only when its operator profile is genuinely distinct and a specialist can share it with a sibling; otherwise merge under one specialist and record the merge

edges.why_related: the tie-break may route a business to a parent category while versioning pressures toward minting a new fine category
edges.resolution_rule: hold at the parent and watch-list until enough businesses cluster to justify a versioned new category under the count band, rather than minting a category for a single ambiguous case

edges.why_related: ranking the dominant activity wants revenue evidence, but revenue is only an unconfirmed estimate, risking a circular or overconfident primary choice
edges.resolution_rule: rank dominant activity from direct public size signals first and use the labeled revenue band only as a tie-breaking hint, never as a stated fact

edges.why_related: stable ids cause specialist assignments to survive renames and splits without re-binding

conflict_axes.name: granularity_vs_sustainability
conflict_axes.description: Finer categories ground sharper specialists but a small market cannot sustain a specialist per micro-category.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: split only when members diverge by operator profile or exceed the count band; otherwise hold or merge

conflict_axes.name: naics_fidelity_vs_local_usefulness
conflict_axes.description: Staying mappable to NAICS aids external data joins but inherits its over-generalization; diverging serves local reality but breaks the join.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: expand past NAICS leaves where Turlock shows a real distinction, but keep a recorded NAICS link for benchmarking

conflict_axes.name: count_band_vs_genuine_distinctness
conflict_axes.description: The count band wants to merge thin categories, but some thin categories are genuinely distinct domains worth their own specialist.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: let distinctness override the lower band only when a specialist can be justified or shared

conflict_axes.name: single_primary_vs_multi_line_reality
conflict_axes.description: One primary keeps ownership clean but a genuinely multi-line business loses visibility in its other categories.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: assign one primary by dominant activity and record secondaries so the business stays visible to sibling categories

conflict_axes.name: estimate_usefulness_vs_honesty
conflict_axes.description: A tighter revenue figure is more useful but per-business revenue is not public, so tightening risks asserting a fabricated fact.
poles: keep an honest wide labeled band
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: always present a labeled wide band tagged estimate-not-actual; never collapse it to a stated figure

conflict_axes.name: community_keyed_vs_neutral_categories
conflict_axes.description: Keying grocers and cuisine to community matches local reality but can mis-handle stores that deliberately serve several communities.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: key by primary community served and record secondary communities rather than forcing a neutral merge

conflict_axes.name: stability_vs_responsiveness
conflict_axes.description: A stable taxonomy is easy to assign against but a responsive one tracks a changing local economy better.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: add categories responsively on discovery but keep ids stable and changes versioned so stability and responsiveness coexist

conflict_axes.name: tie_break_fairness_vs_data_need
conflict_axes.description: Breaking ties toward under-served categories fills data gaps but can distort those categories' true counts.
poles: break ties to fill data gaps
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: use the under-served tie-break only after dominant-activity and FBN-purpose rules fail, and record the reason

conflict_axes.name: append_forward_vs_pruning_obsolete
conflict_axes.description: Never re-generalizing protects real distinctions but leaves dead categories lingering after a niche disappears.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: allow pruning only as an explicit versioned, justified merge, never as a silent re-generalization

edge_cases.description: A panaderia that also runs a taqueria counter spans food retail and a restaurant format
edge_cases.trigger: one storefront sells pan dulce and made-to-order tacos
edge_cases.mitigation: assign the primary by dominant activity from size signals and record the other as a secondary category

edge_cases.description: A market serves Assyrian and Punjabi clientele equally with no clear primary community
edge_cases.trigger: a grocer's inventory and signage straddle two communities
edge_cases.mitigation: apply the tie-break order and key to the primary community while recording the secondary community

edge_cases.description: A one-stop auto shop does general repair, tires, and smog under one roof
edge_cases.trigger: a single shop spans three automotive categories
edge_cases.mitigation: file the primary as the dominant bay-time trade and record tires and smog as secondaries

edge_cases.description: A solo practitioner does tax prep, insurance, and notary work together
edge_cases.trigger: one office blends accounting, insurance, and notary/document services
edge_cases.mitigation: assign the dominant-revenue practice as primary and keep notary/document services distinct from any legal-practice claim

edge_cases.description: A document-preparation business is mistaken for licensed legal practice
edge_cases.trigger: a notario-style office is filed under the legal-practice category
edge_cases.mitigation: keep notary/immigration-doc as its own category and never label it licensed legal practice

edge_cases.description: A revenue benchmark band is read by a downstream consumer as the business's actual revenue
edge_cases.trigger: an estimate band is quoted without its estimate-not-actual tag
edge_cases.mitigation: always carry the estimate-not-actual tag, the confidence level, and the confirming-evidence note with every band

edge_cases.description: A home business has no storefront, no listing, and no FBN filing to categorize from
edge_cases.trigger: a business surfaces with no public footprint
edge_cases.mitigation: mark it unknown and watch-list it rather than inventing data from non-public sources

edge_cases.description: A roaster wholesales beans and also runs a retail cafe counter
edge_cases.trigger: one maker sells B2B and over a retail counter
edge_cases.mitigation: set the primary by dominant channel and record the other channel as a secondary

edge_cases.description: A thin florist category falls below the count band and is tempted into a merge that erases its perishable-supply model
edge_cases.trigger: florist count drops under the lower band
edge_cases.mitigation: keep it distinct under a shared specialist if its operator profile is genuinely different rather than merging it into gifts

edge_cases.description: A new boba/tea-shop cluster appears that no current category holds
edge_cases.trigger: several tea/boba shops open with no fitting category
edge_cases.mitigation: add a versioned new category with a rationale and migrate assignments by stable id once the cluster meets the band

edge_cases.description: A previously justified split is quietly re-merged to simplify the map
edge_cases.trigger: someone proposes collapsing two distinct categories without a version record
edge_cases.mitigation: block any silent re-generalization; require an explicit versioned, justified merge

edge_cases.description: An ambiguous business is forced to a fine leaf instead of held at its parent
edge_cases.trigger: a borderline case is guessed into a leaf category
edge_cases.mitigation: hold at the parent category with a recorded reason and watch-list until signal resolves it

workflow.action: State the taxonomy goal and the specialist-grounding constraint
workflow.description: Fix that each category must be fine enough to ground one specialist and broad enough to hold more than one business
workflow.gate: the goal ties granularity to one-specialist-per-category with both bounds stated

workflow.action: Adopt the NAICS spine and the local-expansion principle
workflow.description: Take NAICS as the floor and declare the granularity-over-generalization expansion rule
workflow.gate: NAICS is named as the spine and at least one local expansion is worked

workflow.action: Set the businesses-per-category band and split/merge triggers
workflow.description: Make split/merge decidable by a count band plus divergence triggers
workflow.artifact: granularity rule with the count band
workflow.gate: a count band and explicit split and merge triggers are stated

workflow.action: Define the naming convention and stable category ids
workflow.description: Assign a mutable display name plus an immutable stable id per category
workflow.gate: every category carries an immutable id distinct from its display name

workflow.action: Split each domain into granular local categories
workflow.description: Apply the granularity rule across food, grocery, restaurant, personal-care, automotive, health, professional, retail, contractor, ag, hobby, and production domains
workflow.gate: each domain split names its distinct categories with the separating signal, ag/dairy-support included as first-class

workflow.action: Assign each business a primary plus optional secondary categories
workflow.description: Choose the primary by dominant public-signal activity and record secondaries
workflow.gate: each multi-line business has exactly one primary and recorded secondaries

workflow.action: Resolve ambiguous assignments with the tie-break protocol
workflow.description: Apply the ordered tie-breaks and the parent-category fallback with a recorded reason
workflow.gate: every ambiguous call uses the ordered tie-breaks and records its reason

workflow.action: Estimate scale as a labeled benchmark band
workflow.description: Scale a category benchmark by public size signals into a low/high estimate band
workflow.gate: every band carries an estimate-not-actual tag, a confidence level, and a confirming-evidence note

workflow.description: Confirm every datum is public and no actual revenue or private owner data is used
workflow.gate: no actual-revenue claim and no owner data beyond public FBN filings exist

workflow.action: Map each category to exactly one owning specialist
workflow.description: Bind categories to specialists one-to-one, bundling only genuinely thin siblings
workflow.gate: every category has exactly one owner and bundles contain only thin related siblings

workflow.action: Version the taxonomy forward on discovery
workflow.description: Add new categories with version stamps and forbid silent re-generalization
workflow.gate: additions are versioned and migrated by stable id with no silent re-merges

dominance_rules.rule: The public-data honesty floor dominates every assignment and estimate
dominance_rules.rationale: no usefulness justifies stating a fabricated revenue or exposing private owner data
dominance_rules.trigger: any datum that is non-public or any actual-revenue claim for a named business
dominance_rules.action: reject the datum and fall back to a labeled estimate or an unknown mark

dominance_rules.rule: Estimate-not-actual labeling dominates any revenue figure
dominance_rules.rationale: an unlabeled band reads as a fact and breaks the honesty contract
dominance_rules.trigger: a revenue band presented without its estimate tag
dominance_rules.action: block it until the tag, confidence, and confirming-evidence note are attached

dominance_rules.rule: The specialist-grounding goal dominates category boundary choices
dominance_rules.rationale: categories exist to be owned by a specialist, so boundaries follow ownership coherence
dominance_rules.trigger: a proposed split or merge that no specialist can coherently own
dominance_rules.action: re-draw the boundary so each resulting category is briefable to one specialist

dominance_rules.rule: Genuine operator-profile distinctness dominates the lower count band
dominance_rules.rationale: merging a truly distinct domain to clear a count threshold erases a real specialist need
dominance_rules.trigger: a sub-band category that is genuinely distinct
dominance_rules.action: keep it distinct under a shared specialist rather than merging away the distinction

dominance_rules.rule: Dominant public-signal activity dominates the primary-category choice
dominance_rules.rationale: ownership must rest on the observable main line, not a guessed or estimated one
dominance_rules.trigger: a multi-line business needing a primary
dominance_rules.action: assign the primary by dominant size-signal activity, with the revenue band only a tie-break hint

dominance_rules.rule: The legal/regulatory line dominates convenience in the notary-versus-legal split
dominance_rules.rationale: conflating document services with licensed legal practice misrepresents a regulated role
dominance_rules.trigger: a notary/document business near the legal-practice category
dominance_rules.action: keep it in its own category and never label it licensed legal practice

dominance_rules.rule: Versioned, justified change dominates silent re-generalization
dominance_rules.rationale: silent re-merging destroys real distinctions and history
dominance_rules.trigger: a proposed merge of previously split categories
dominance_rules.action: require an explicit version stamp and justification or reject the merge

dominance_rules.rationale: the local backbone must be first-class, not buried under generic retail or services
dominance_rules.trigger: an ag/dairy-support business about to be filed under a generic category
dominance_rules.action: place it in its first-class ag/dairy-support category instead

anti_rework_rules.rule: Assign an immutable stable id at category creation
anti_rework_rules.prevents: orphaned assignments when a category is later renamed, split, or merged

anti_rework_rules.rule: Record a recorded NAICS link even when expanding past the leaf
anti_rework_rules.prevents: losing the external benchmark join needed for revenue estimation later

anti_rework_rules.rule: Record secondary categories at first assignment, not after
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a multi-line business vanishing from its sibling categories and needing re-discovery

anti_rework_rules.rule: Attach the estimate-not-actual tag the moment a revenue band is created
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a band later being quoted as a fact and having to be retracted

anti_rework_rules.rule: Keep notary/immigration-doc distinct from legal practice from the start
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a costly re-classification and misrepresentation of a regulated role

anti_rework_rules.rule: Hold genuinely ambiguous businesses at the parent category with a reason
anti_rework_rules.prevents: guessing a fine leaf and re-filing once real signal arrives

anti_rework_rules.rule: Version every category addition or merge when it happens
anti_rework_rules.prevents: an undocumented map that cannot be audited or rolled back

anti_rework_rules.rule: Check each new category against the specialist map before finalizing
anti_rework_rules.prevents: minting an unownable category that must be re-merged later

iteration_protocol.trigger: a new business cluster is discovered that no category holds
iteration_protocol.action: evaluate it against the count band and add a versioned new category if justified

iteration_protocol.trigger: a category grows past the upper count band or divides by operator profile
iteration_protocol.action: split it and re-map the resulting categories to specialists

iteration_protocol.trigger: a category falls below the lower band
iteration_protocol.action: test genuine distinctness and either hold, share a specialist, or version a justified merge

iteration_protocol.trigger: a multi-line business's dominant activity shifts
iteration_protocol.action: re-rank primary and secondary categories and re-map ownership

iteration_protocol.trigger: a category benchmark or a public size signal updates
iteration_protocol.action: re-estimate the affected revenue bands keeping the estimate-not-actual label

iteration_protocol.trigger: a new public data source becomes available
iteration_protocol.action: re-confirm assignments and refresh estimates within the public-data floor

iteration_protocol.trigger: the specialist roster changes (a specialist is added, retired, or overloaded)
iteration_protocol.action: re-balance the category-to-specialist map and re-test thin-sibling bundles

priority_rationale: The goal, base scheme, granularity rule, and naming convention come first because every category split and every assignment depends on them; the per-domain splits and the primary/secondary assignment build the actual map; revenue estimation and the public-data guardrail bound how scale may be expressed; and the specialist map and versioning come last because they bind the finished map to owners and keep it accurate over time.
